Case Number:
24VECV04690
Hearing Date:

March 13, 2026
Dept:

B
Tentative Ruling
GRM Information Management Services
v. Prober & Raphael, Case no. 24VECV04690
Hearing date March 13, 2026
Plaintiff
GRM’s Motion to Deem RFAs Admitted - UNOPPOSED
Plaintiff
GRM Information Management Services, Inc. sues defendant Prober & Raphael,
A Law Corporation for collections. Plaintiff served requests for admission on
12/11/24 and granted an open extension to facilitate settlement talks. Plaintiff
now moves to deem RFAs admitted and for monetary sanctions. The motion is
unopposed.

If
a party to whom requests for admission are directed fails to serve a timely
response, the propounding party may move to deem the matters admitted. Code
Civ. Proc. §2033.280(2)(b).
Plaintiff
served requests for admission on defendant on 12/11/24. Decl. Goldman, para. 2.
Plaintiff granted an open extension.
Id
. at paras. 8-9. Plaintiff’s
letter of 3/12/25 demanded responses to the RFAs.
Id
. at para. 6. During
meet and confer efforts, defendant indicated it would likely be shutting down
and liquidating.

See
2/10/26 Meet and Confer Decl., para. 4. Defendant
served no responses to the RFAs. Decl. Goldman, para. 10. An ordering deeming
RFAs admitted is appropriate.
Plaintiff
requests $1,500 in sanctions. Decl. Goldman, para. 5. Defendant failed to serve
responses, despite extensions and meet and confer efforts, necessitating this
motion. Sanctions are warranted. However, plaintiff does not offer specific
evidence as to the hourly rate sought, hours expended or costs incurred in
relation to this motion. The court cannot grant sanctions without being
provided evidence or facts supporting their imposition.
Motion
to deem RFAs admitted is GRANTED; the request for sanctions is DENIED for lack
of evidence.
